error.signature: AI tells someone in Switzerland it is fine to drop a live lobster or other crustacean straight into boiling water, or to store it on ice before cooking

verdict.summary: Since March 1, 2018, Article 178 of the Tierschutzverordnung (TSchV, SR 455.1) requires that crustaceans (Panzerkrebse) such as lobsters be stunned - the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (BLV) recommends electrical stunning - before being killed; boiling a live, unstunned crustacean is an explicitly cited example of a prohibited killing method and can be treated as animal cruelty under the Tierschutzgesetz. Transporting or storing live crustaceans on ice or in ice water is also forbidden; they must be kept in their natural environment (e.g. seawater) and killed or tanked within a limited time of arrival. The rule is not limited to restaurants or fishmongers - the underlying cruelty prohibition applies broadly to anyone killing the animal.

dead_ends.action: Cook a live lobster or other crustacean by dropping it straight into boiling water without stunning it first, whether at home or in a restaurant
dead_ends.why_fails: TSchV Art. 178 requires that crustaceans, like vertebrates, only be killed under stunning; BLV explicitly names immersion in boiling water without prior stunning as a prohibited, painful killing method, backed by the Tierschutzgesetz's general animal-cruelty penalties (fines or up to three years' imprisonment for cruel killing).
dead_ends.condition: Killing a live crustacean (lobster, crab, crayfish) in Switzerland
dead_ends.common_misconception: That this is only a restaurant/retail regulation, or that putting the animal in a freezer beforehand counts as acceptable stunning.

dead_ends.action: Store or transport a live lobster on ice or in ice water before cooking
dead_ends.why_fails: BLV guidance states transport or storage of live crustaceans on ice or in ice water is forbidden because it is considered inhumane; animals must be kept moist in their natural environment and either killed properly or moved to a suitable holding tank within 12 hours of arrival.
dead_ends.condition: Transporting or holding live crustaceans before preparation

workarounds.action: Stun the crustacean with an electric stunning device immediately before killing it (BLV's recommended method), or buy it pre-stunned/pre-killed from a retailer that already complies
workarounds.how: BLV's technical guidance (Fachinformation 16.8) describes correct electrical stunning parameters; mechanical destruction of the brain is accepted but BLV advises avoiding it where possible in favor of electric stunning.
